questions.stem: Where do you see when an import semantic model last refreshed and whether the refresh failed?

options.text: The eventstream's data insights
The semantic model's refresh history
The Git panel
The lakehouse's table history

questions.explanation: A semantic model's refresh history lists each scheduled and on-demand refresh with its status and details.

questions.stem: At Fernway, what does refreshing the Direct Lake semantic model do after the nightly load?

options.text: It deletes old rows
It imports a full copy of the table into the model
It reframes the model to the latest version of the Delta table, a metadata operation that doesn't copy the data
It rewrites the Delta table

questions.explanation: For Direct Lake, a refresh (framing) points the model at the latest table version. It's quick and cheap because no data is imported.

questions.stem: The semantic model must refresh right after the pipeline that loads its data finishes, not at a fixed time. What do you add?

options.text: A shortcut to the model
A deployment rule
A Semantic model refresh activity at the end of the pipeline
A second schedule an hour later

questions.explanation: The Semantic model refresh activity refreshes a model as a pipeline step, so it runs only after the load succeeds.

questions.stem: An import semantic model's scheduled refresh has failed several nights in a row, and now it doesn't run at all. What happened?

options.text: The model was deleted
The capacity was paused by Microsoft
Power BI deactivated the schedule after repeated consecutive failures; fix the cause and turn the schedule back on
The refresh moved to Direct Lake by itself

questions.explanation: After four consecutive failures Power BI deactivates the refresh schedule. Check the refresh history for the error, fix it, and re-enable the schedule.

questions.stem: A Direct Lake on SQL analytics endpoint semantic model's refresh succeeds but shows a warning, and report queries have become slower. A table has grown past a guardrail and fallback is enabled. What is happening?

options.text: The model is falling back to DirectQuery mode for queries
The model is loading the table in Import mode until the next refresh
The model is returning cached results from the last successful refresh
The model is skipping the oversized table and returning partial results

questions.explanation: For Direct Lake on SQL, exceeding a guardrail makes the model fall back to DirectQuery when fallback is enabled: refresh succeeds with a warning and queries still work but more slowly. It doesn't switch to Import or skip the table.

questions.stem: A Direct Lake on OneLake semantic model's refresh fails after a Delta table grew past the model's guardrail limits. What must you do so the model can be queried again?

options.text: Delete the model's refresh history
Optimize the Delta tables so that they fall within the guardrail limits
Enable DirectQuery fallback on the model
Switch the model to a larger capacity's shared workspace

questions.explanation: For Direct Lake on OneLake, exceeding guardrails makes refresh fail, and the model can't be queried until the Delta tables are optimized to fit the limits. Fallback to DirectQuery applies to Direct Lake on SQL, not Direct Lake on OneLake.

questions.stem: You use Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop to check whether a visual on a Direct Lake model is served in Direct Lake mode. What tells you that the model fell back?

options.text: The visual shows a Visual display metric only
The visual shows a Direct query performance metric
The visual shows a DAX query time of zero
The visual's row count is shown in red

questions.explanation: If the model falls back to DirectQuery to process the visual's DAX query, Performance Analyzer shows a Direct query metric. A visual without DirectQuery processing was handled in Direct Lake mode.

questions.stem: You trace a Direct Lake semantic model with SQL Server Profiler while users open a report. Which two statements about the trace are correct? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Any EngineEdition query in the trace proves that the model fell back
DirectQuery_Begin and DirectQuery_End events suggest that the model might have fallen back to DirectQuery
VertiPaq SE query events show that the query fell back to DirectQuery
VertiPaq SE query events show that the query was processed in Direct Lake mode
Direct Lake queries produce no events at all in a Profiler trace

questions.explanation: DirectQuery Begin/End events point to a possible fallback, and VertiPaq storage engine events indicate Direct Lake processing. EngineEdition and OLS checks always use DirectQuery and don't mean a fallback.

questions.stem: Reports on a Direct Lake on SQL analytics endpoint model are slow on one table only. That table is based on a SQL view in the warehouse. What is the likely reason?

options.text: Direct Lake can't load data from a SQL view, so queries on that table fall back to DirectQuery
SQL views disable V-Order on the underlying tables
SQL views are copied into Import mode at each refresh, which slows the queries
SQL views make the model refresh only once per day

questions.explanation: Direct Lake on SQL analytics endpoints falls back to DirectQuery when the source is a SQL view, because it can't load the data directly from a Delta table. A lakehouse materialized view creates Delta tables and avoids this.

questions.stem: A Power Automate flow refreshes an import semantic model after a load. The refresh failed, but the model owner got no failure email, although failure notifications are turned on. Why?

options.text: Failure emails are only sent after three consecutive failures
Failure emails are only sent for models on shared capacity
Failure emails are only sent to users outside the tenant
Refreshes triggered programmatically, such as through Power Automate, don't trigger email notifications

questions.explanation: On-demand and programmatically triggered refreshes don't send failure emails; notifications apply to scheduled refresh. External users can't be recipients at all.
